issues.description: The problem statement instructs that the SealSaloon should have a final Stock field initialized in the constructor (instance initialization), but also explicitly requires that the stock attribute be static and shared across all instances. Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is not appropriate and creates a contradiction: a static final field must be initialized in a static context (declaration or static initializer) or at the point of declaration, not in the instance constructor. This contradicts the construction guidance and will confuse students about where and how to declare/initialize the stock attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction by choosing one approach and update the problem statement (and any examples): either (A) require stock to be an instance final field and initialize it in the no-arg constructor, or (B) require stock to be static (shared) and state it should be declared static final and initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Update the instructions to explicitly state the chosen initialization location and explain that static fields cannot be initialized in an instance constructor.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient name field is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template repository defines getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify exact getter names, which leaves ambiguity. This mismatch means students comparing template and solution (or trying to follow solution code patterns) must map two different method names to the same conceptual getter, creating unnecessary cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent getter name for the StockIngredient name field across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the template getter getIngredientName() to getName() (and update any call sites like Stock.findStockIngredient to use getName()), or alternatively rename the solution getter to getIngredientName() everywhere. Update the problem statement to state the exact getter naming convention (e.g., getName()) to avoid ambiguity.
